title: Musk Says Hiring Jensen Huang Would Be an ‘Honor’
author: Xebec
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Elon Musk has said it would be an “honor” to hire Jensen Huang, offering support to Nvidia’s embattled chief executive as the chipmaker’s board considers his future following reports of multiple extramarital affairs.

“That would be an honor,” Musk wrote on X in response to a post urging him to recruit Huang. The comment signalled admiration for the Nvidia cofounder, although it did not amount to a formal job offer or identify a potential role.

The exchange came amid reports that Nvidia’s directors were weighing whether Huang should remain in charge. The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to consider his removal, while other reports described efforts to explore possible successors.

Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, according to published accounts. The controversy intensified after The New York Times reported an alleged relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell had not confirmed that report, according to the International Business Times.

The allegations followed scrutiny of Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed. Reports have linked her to suspected Chinese intelligence activity. Those claims remain allegations; China has denied them. Nvidia’s board has said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised, while pledging an independent investigation.

Musk’s intervention reflects longstanding business ties. His companies buy Nvidia processors used to develop artificial intelligence, and he has praised Huang’s leadership.

For Nvidia, the reported deliberations raise questions about governance and succession at a company central to the global AI industry. Musk’s response adds another dimension: a departing Huang could potentially find support from one of Nvidia’s biggest customers. Any hiring discussions, board decision or leadership transition would require separate confirmation beyond Musk’s brief social media response.
